sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Florence, AZ?
sections.html:
A Florence owner can sell quickly by accepting a cash offer on the house as it stands, or can list the house and wait for a buyer who needs a loan. The right pick depends on repairs, timing and whether anyone lives in the home. Workers in Florence report a mean commute of 30.9 minutes, a detail some buyers weigh when they compare towns.

  • Cash sale as-is: fits inherited property, a house with deferred repairs, a rental with tenants, or an owner who must relocate.
  • Agent listing: fits a move-in ready house where the owner can handle showings and a buyer's inspection period.
  • Owner sale: fits sellers who already have a buyer in mind and can manage the contract and title steps.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures show an 86.8% owner-occupied rate in Florence and a median home value of $346,300. Median gross rent is $1,302. The median value is lower than the $471,300 reported for Goodyear and the $575,100 reported for Gilbert, so compare your own sale price and repair estimates before choosing a route.

sections.h2: What is Florence, Arizona like, and what shaped it?
sections.html:
Florence is the county seat of Pinal County, on the south bank of the Gila River at an elevation of about 1,539 feet. The Census Bureau estimates 25,222 residents as of July 1, 2025 and about 62.6 square miles of land, up from 52.5 square miles in 2010. State Routes 79 and 287 serve the town.

Levi Ruggles surveyed the townsite in the 1860s and secured a post office in 1866. Silver found in 1875 led to the Silver King Mine, and canals dug in the 1880s let farming and ranching grow. The town includes a National Historic District with more than 25 buildings on the National Register of Historic Places, the original Main Street townsite was listed on October 26, 1982, and Florence High School, built in 1887, is listed as well. The Territorial Prison opened in 1909 after the Yuma prison closed, and the town now hosts several state, federal, county and private prisons.

The Census count shows 6,719 households averaging 2.39 people, which comes to roughly 16,000 residents, while the headline population is 25,222. For a seller, the household count is the better guide to how many homes compete for buyers. Newer development has arrived too, including an Anthem community by Pulte and Del Webb about six miles northwest of the old townsite. The climate is lower Sonoran Desert, with a monsoon season that brings flash flood risk and afternoon thunderstorms, and winter storms that supply the other half of annual rain.

sections.h2: How does the Florence Historic District affect a house sale?
sections.html:
A house inside the Florence Historic District may carry preservation compliance steps, so a seller should learn early whether the address falls within it. The Town's historic preservation staff works with the Historic District Advisory Commission, homeowners, developers and the State Historic Preservation Office on preservation laws, compliance procedures, rehabilitation standards and financial incentives.

The Town also runs events such as a Walking Tour and a Historic District Home Tour. If you own an older house in town, ask the Town's Community Development Department two questions before listing: whether the property is in the district, and whether any planned repair, such as new windows or a new porch, triggers a compliance step.

sections.h2: When are Pinal County property taxes due for a Florence home?
sections.html:
Pinal County bills Florence property in two halves, with the first due October 1 and the second due March 1. Under the Treasurer's schedule the first half turns delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 1, and the second half after 5 p.m. on May 1. Because November 1, 2026 fell on a Sunday, the deadline moved to the next business day, and that date has passed. A bill of $100 or less is due October 1 in full.

  • Late payment carries a penalty of 16% a year, prorated monthly, and the Treasurer says interest cannot be waived.
  • Paying the full year by December 31 avoids interest on the first half.
  • Unpaid taxes can send a parcel to the online tax lien sale each February.
  • The Treasurer mails bills as a courtesy in September and is not required to, so keep your mailing address current with the Assessor at 520-866-6361.

Tell the escrow officer your tax status when you open escrow so the closing statement splits the year correctly. The Treasurer's main office is in Florence, and the Assessor keeps offices in Florence, Apache Junction, Casa Grande, Maricopa and San Tan Valley.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Florence property valuation?
sections.html:
You appeal by filing a petition for review with the Pinal County Assessor within 60 days of the date the Notice of Value was mailed, and filing is free. The Assessor mails notices by March 1, uses Form 82130R for residential property, and must rule on every petition by August 15. You may ask for an optional meeting with the appraisers.

Only the full cash value can be appealed, because taxes rest on the limited property value, which in most cases cannot rise more than 5% a year. If the limited value already sits below the market value you believe is right, a win will not lower the tax. After an Assessor denial, a second level is available at the Pinal County Board of Equalization within 25 days, and a further appeal can go to court within 60 days of the last decision. Taxes on a parcel in a court appeal must be paid before they become delinquent, or the court dismisses the case.

sections.h2: What happens at the Pinal County Recorder when a Florence house sells?
sections.html:
The deed for a Florence sale is recorded at the Pinal County Recorder's Office, 31 N Pinal Street, Building E, Florence. The phone is 520-866-6830. Documents can be recorded in person, by mail or through the county's approved electronic recording partners, and most sales reach the recorder through the title company.

  • The Recorder's FAQ says buyers and sellers must complete the affidavit of property value, and that failing to do so is a class 2 misdemeanor. If a transfer qualifies for an exemption, the deed carries a notation such as A.R.S. 11-1134 B3 instead.
  • Since September 14, 2026, anyone presenting a document in person must show valid government photo identification. Escrow and title companies, banks, active State Bar members and government agencies are exempt.
  • Copies of recorded documents cost $1 per page, with $3 more for certification.
  • The Assessor's Parcel Alert List sends a free notice when a new deed is received for your parcel, a guard against deed fraud.

Statute sets the recording fee at $30 per instrument, which includes a $2 transfer fee. The Recorder's Office cannot prepare documents or give legal advice.

sections.h2: What should Florence landlords and hosts check before selling?
sections.html:
Landlords should confirm the house is registered with the Pinal County Assessor, since the Town of Florence states that all Arizona counties require residential rental registration. A.R.S. 33-1902 backs this up by barring occupancy of unregistered rental property and requiring updates within ten days of a change.

Short-term rentals of 29 days or less fall under the state's transient lodging classification and the Town's hotel classification for transaction privilege tax. The Arizona Department of Revenue administers Florence's tax program, and its taxpayer line is 800-352-4090. Hosts should settle any back filings before they close, because underreported tax can bring interest and penalties.

faqs.q: Which county records a deed after a Florence sale?
faqs.a: Pinal County. The Pinal County Recorder's Office at 31 N Pinal Street, Building E in Florence records the deed, and the office can be reached at 520-866-6830. Most sales are submitted by the title or escrow company.

faqs.q: Do I need photo ID to record a document in Florence?
faqs.a: Yes, if you present it in person at the Pinal County Recorder. Since September 14, 2026 a valid government photo ID is required unless you are an escrow or title company, a bank or credit union, an active State Bar member or a government agency.

faqs.q: When do Pinal County taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: The first half goes delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 1 and the second half after 5 p.m. on May 1. Late payments accrue 16% interest a year, prorated monthly, and interest cannot be waived.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Florence home's value?
faqs.a: You have 60 days from the mailing date of the Notice of Value to file a petition with the Pinal County Assessor. There is no filing fee, and the Assessor must rule by August 15.

faqs.q: Does Florence have a historic district?
faqs.a: Yes. Florence has a National Historic District with more than 25 buildings on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Town's preservation staff and Historic District Advisory Commission work with homeowners on compliance procedures and rehabilitation standards.
